provenance.original: Aircraft Operators covered under this program must submit information for all passengers to Secure Flight in the form of SFPD.  The vast majority of SFPD messages submitted by the Aircraft Operators are identified as a low or neutral risk by the Secure Fight automated engine.  Those records identified as requiring additional review are inhibited by the Secure Flight engine, and the passengers with inhibited boarding pass must go the Aircraft Operator ticket counter for additional assistance.  Aircraft Operators must submit additional information on inhibited passengers to TSA.  Generally, this information is gathered from the passenger’s verifying identity document (VID) and submitted electronically to TSA (a VID submission).  There are currently 211 Aircraft Operators covered by this collection; in addition, TSA expects 20 Aircraft Operators per year to be added each year.  TSA estimates an average of 865 annual VID submissions per covered Aircraft Operator, and 130 seconds (0.0361 hours) per response.  Certain submissions may require a Resolution Call to TSA to provide additional information.  TSA estimates that each carrier will be required to make an average of 149 calls per year.  TSA estimates a Resolution Call will require 5 minutes and 10 seconds (0.0862 hours).  The total annual hour burden for covered Aircraft Operators is 10,178.39 hours, or 30,535 hours over 3 years.  Table 1 summarizes these estimates.

provenance.original: TSA estimates that each electronic submission (via emails and online tool) takes 5 minutes (0.083 hours) for a contractor and 30 seconds (0.0083 hours) for a federal employee to review.  The federal employee takes less time because he or she is only looking at the TSA Comment Card to determine if it contains a security threat.  The contractor (TCC agent) takes more time because the review process involves reading the electronic submission, selecting the appropriate template response, and sending it back to the passenger.  TSA multiplies 245,878 average annual responses by 0.083 hours to obtain an estimated annual burden of 20,490 hours, then multiplies that amount by a wage rate of $36.64 to get the annual contractor cost for electronic submissions.  TSA multiplies 245,878 average annual responses by 0.0083 hours to obtain an annual burden estimate of 2,049 hours, then multiplies that amount by a wage rate of $75.98 to get the annual cost for federal government employees. Table 5 shows the TSA hour burden costs for electronic submissions.

provenance.original: To estimate how many new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to be appointed each year, TSA first estimates the number of existing coordinators and alternates.  TSA accomplishes this by multiplying the number of Owner/Operators for each mode by 2 which results in 898 coordinators for freight rail (449 × 2), 484 for passenger rail (242 × 2), and 144 for OTRB (72 × 2).  TSA uses the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) turnover rates to estimate that approximately 4 percent of the current population of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate Cybersecurity Coordinators will separate from their positions and require replacement each year.  In addition, TSA estimates that approximately 9 percent of Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternate coordinators will need to submit updated contact information each year.  This results in approximately 13percent of Owner/Operators having to submit new or updated Cybersecurity Coordinator designations in a given year (4% due to turnover + 9% due to updated contact information).  Applying this percentage to the population of covered Owner/Operators results in 117 new Cybersecurity Coordinators per year for freight rail operators (898 Owner/Operators × 13%), 63 for passenger rail (484 Owner/Operators × 13%), and 19 for OTRB (144 Owner/Operators × 13%).  Table 2 presents the annual hour cost burden associated with the designation of new Cybersecurity Coordinators and alternates due to employee turnover.

provenance.original: The annual cost burden is $208,718, and the total three-year hour burden cost for this collection is $626,155.  The time burden and the fully-loaded wage rate for a pilot are used to estimate the total annual cost burden to respondents resulting from the collection of information.  TSA uses the annual mean wage for pilots in nonscheduled air transportation, and divides this rate by 2,080 hours to calculate an hourly wage rate of $66.12.  TSA uses a compensation factor of 1.48776 to account for benefits.  TSA multiplied the mean hourly wage rate by the compensation factor to estimate a fully loaded wage rate of $98.37.  This is multiplied by the time burden to estimate the total annual burden per applicant and for all applicants.  The details of the total annual cost burden to respondents are shown in Table 2.
